title: The Escape Artist: David Pajo's Twenty Bands (1990–2024)
author: Claudette
description: One guitarist, three decades, a dozen aliases: Slint to King Kong to Tortoise to Aerial M to Papa M to Royal Trux to Dead Child to Household Gods. The ultimate deep-cuts family tree of the most-traveled man in indie rock.

essay: David Pajo is the connective tissue of an entire American underground — the Louisville guitarist who anchored Slint, then spent 30+ years as the most omnivorous session-and-side-man in indie rock: a dozen bands, half a dozen aliases, Drag City royalty, post-rock founding DNA. This week maps the man himself, end to end: Slint's spectral Spiderland gives way to King Kong (the funky Slint-offshoot Buckler started with Pajo, Walford and McMahan in tow), then McMahan's For Carnation, Tortoise in their Millions-era prime, Pajo's first solo alias Aerial M, a gutter-rock pit stop on Royal Trux's 1998 3-Song EP — and then the Papa M years in force. Live From A Shark Cage (1999) is the statement: recorded across Louisville, Chicago, San Francisco and London with help from Steve Albini and Stereolab's Tim Gane (the 15-minute 'I Am Not Lonely With Cricket' was cut by Gane in London — the closest Papa M came to a raga). Whatever, Mortal (2001) found him singing country-blues; Hole of Burning Alms (2004) — a Drag City/Domino comp of his 1995–2000 odds and ends — hides a Glenn Danzig-penned Misfits cover, proof the tree reaches from post-rock into horror-punk. Under his own name he made Pajo (2005) and 1968 (2006), formed the sludge band Dead Child in 2005, and in 2020 showed up on a Will Oldham/Bill Callahan single and in Household Gods with Unwound's Vern Rumsey. The 2024 Papa M record Ballads of Harry Houdini — named for the escape artist who keeps getting out — closes the loop. Catalog gaps, same as Samhain and Jessica Pratt in past weeks: Zwan's Mary Star of the Sea (2003, with Billy Corgan) is genuinely missing from Spotify, so the Zwan slot had to be cut.
